title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 55 (Issue and Redemption of Preference Shares)

content.overview: Section 55 restricts a company limited by shares from issuing irredeemable preference shares. Preference shares must be redeemable within a period not exceeding twenty years from the date of issue (with a longer period permitted for infrastructure projects as prescribed). Redemption must be out of profits available for dividend or out of the proceeds of a fresh issue, and fully paid-up shares only may be redeemed. A capital redemption reserve is required where redemption is out of profits.
content.glance: No irredeemable preference shares; redeem within 20 years (infrastructure exception); redeem only fully paid shares out of profits or fresh issue; capital redemption reserve when out of profits.
content.study: A company limited by shares cannot issue any preference shares which are irredeemable. Preference shares must be liable to be redeemed within a period not exceeding twenty years from the date of their issue; for infrastructure projects a longer period not exceeding thirty years may be prescribed with conditions. Preference shares may be redeemed only out of the profits of the company which would otherwise be available for dividend or out of the proceeds of a fresh issue of shares made for the purposes of redemption; only fully paid-up shares may be redeemed. Where shares are redeemed out of profits, a sum equal to the nominal amount of the shares redeemed must be transferred to a capital redemption reserve account. Current-law framing: confirm no irredeemable issue; check redemption period, source of funds and CRR if applicable.

sections.heading: No Irredeemable Preference Shares
sections.body: A company limited by shares shall not issue irredeemable preference shares.

sections.heading: Redemption Period
sections.body: Preference shares must be redeemable within twenty years of issue; infrastructure projects may have a longer prescribed period up to thirty years.

sections.heading: Source of Redemption
sections.body: Redemption only out of profits available for dividend or proceeds of a fresh issue; only fully paid-up shares may be redeemed.

sections.heading: Capital Redemption Reserve
sections.body: Where redemption is out of profits, a sum equal to the nominal amount redeemed must be transferred to the capital redemption reserve account.

provisions.title: Issue and redemption of preference shares

examples.title: Valid redeemable issue
examples.body: A company issues preference shares redeemable in 15 years, to be redeemed out of profits with CRR created. Section 55 is complied with.

examples.title: Irredeemable attempt
examples.body: Articles purport to authorise irredeemable preference shares. Section 55 prohibits such issue.

hypotheticals.question: Can preference shares be perpetual under the 2013 Act?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 55 bans irredeemable preference shares and requires redemption within the statutory period.

distinctions.title: Redeemable preference (s. 55) vs kinds of capital (s. 43)
distinctions.left: Issue and redemption rules for preference shares

misconceptions.trap: Preference shares can be made irredeemable by special resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Section 55 prohibits issue of irredeemable preference shares by a company limited by shares.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 55 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm company limited by shares. II. Check redeemability and period. III. Test source of funds and CRR. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Issue terms; redemption period; funding source; CRR; precise relief.

examTips: CRR when redeeming out of profits.
